summary: A collection of sneaky, kid-approved recipes shared by parents who hide vegetables in foods picky eaters love, such as pizza sauce, quinoa, smoothies, mac and cheese, pudding, pancakes, wraps, and dips. Each entry is dated from September to December 2023 and features a named parent, a signature dish, and a playful presentation trick. The note frames feeding picky eaters as a creative, good-humored game of nourishment and disguise.
one_line: Parents share dated, playful recipes that hide vegetables in kid-favorite foods like pizza, mac and cheese, smoothies, pancakes, and dips.
key_facts: Emily Thompson, mom of twin picky eaters, made a pizza 'super sauce' on September 4, 2023 from roasted red peppers, cherry tomatoes, carrots and zucchini, all pureed.
Emily Thompson serves her veggie pizza on a whole-wheat crust, with bell peppers shaped into stars and olives into smiley faces.
Todd Benson, a self-proclaimed 'Grain Magician', revealed his 'Cheesy Quinoa Monsters' on October 15; they use mascarpone cheese, quinoa, and natural food coloring to make a green goo.
Todd Benson serves his quinoa monsters in individual cups with funny face garnishes.
Sara Kim's 'Purple Potions of Power' are blueberry-banana smoothies hiding avocados and spinach, poured on September 28, 2023 and topped with chia seeds.
Janet Lee revealed on November 1, 2023 a mac and cheese made with cooked, pureed cauliflower; her twins don't notice it.
Marcus Green shared 'Chocolate Clouds of Mystery' on December 20, 2023, a chocolate pudding made creamy with hidden avocados.
Lucy O'Donnell's pancakes (September 22, 2023) contain oats and mashed bananas and are topped with Greek yogurt and fruit faces, such as raspberry hair and kiwi-slice eyes.
Kelly Sanchez's 'Superhero Roll-Up' (October 10, 2023) is a whole grain tortilla with turkey, cheese, and a thin sliver of hidden spinach.
Dan Thompson's 'Dare-to-Dip' sauce (September 12, 2023) blends roasted eggplant, Greek yogurt, and a hint of lemon, disguised as ranch dip.
Dan Thompson presents broccoli as a 'tree' to encourage kids to dip and eat vegetables.
The note's closing theme is that creativity can turn dinner from a battlefield into a playground.
